弾.meaning: An archer finds his <part>bow</part> far too slow, so he invents something <part>simple</part>: he bends it backwards and flicks dried peas off the string. They whistle across the field and punch through a fence. Each pea flies like a <kanji>bullet</kanji>.
弾.on: One pea zips down the stairs into the <sound>dun</sound>geon and rings off the bars.
弾.kun: Later he props the bow on his <sound>hee</sound>l and strums its string: tonight he plays it like a harp.

犯.meaning: A tiny <part>seahorse</part> picks the lock of its tank with a bent <part>fishhook</part>, swims through the pipes and empties the aquarium's tip jar. By dawn it's back home, innocent face on. It's the perfect <kanji>crime</kanji>.
犯.on: The only clue is a sticky trail of <sound>hon</sound>ey along the pipes.
犯.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the old <sound>ca</sound>rp in the next tank, who saw it all.

伸.meaning: A shop hangs its wooden <part>monkey sign</part> from a <part>coat hook</part> by the door. Every night the painted monkey's arms grow a little longer, until they wrap round the whole street. The sign just keeps getting bigger; watch it <kanji>expand</kanji>.
伸.on: The long arms even reach a passer-by and give his <sound>shin</sound> a cheeky kick.
伸.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' squeals the shopkeeper as the arms stretch right round the corner.

刑.meaning: A sailor has stolen from the captain's cabin. His sentence: jump the same <part>hurdle</part> on deck all afternoon, while the bosun taps a blunt <part>dagger</part> on the ship's bell every time he slows down. On this ship, that's how they <kanji>punish</kanji> thieves.
刑.on: And what did he steal? Not gold, but the captain's birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke.

像.meaning: In the town square a stone <part>elephant</part> stands so still that everyone uses its curled trunk as a <part>coat hook</part>. Hats, scarves and umbrellas dangle from it all winter. At midnight it sighs and shakes them off, but by day it's a <kanji>statue</kanji> again.
像.on: Round its plinth a <sound>zo</sound>diac wheel is carved, and it stands on its own sign.

挙.meaning: In a classroom, <part>eight</part> pupils all know the answer. Each <part>hand</part> shoots up so fast that a <part>sparkle</part> crackles at the fingertips. The teacher has to wear sunglasses every time they <kanji>raise</kanji> them.
挙.on: He buys the sunglasses from a little <sound>kio</sound>sk at the back of the room.
挙.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! Me! Me!' they shout, stretching higher and higher.
